what: The store built its whole index table (a walk of every row, a sort, 64 bytes a row) inside a commit on the daemon's loop every 65,536 new records; at one value an item that is every crate or two.
whys: The table was built where the commit that names it is made, so the head and the table agree by construction.
That agreement was stated nowhere as an invariant, so nothing said a table could be older than its head.
The head had one meaning for a pack's indexed end: the end at the write.
Work on the loop had no rule tying its cost to something bounded (packs), only to 'once per 65,536 records'.
Record counts were sized for one value a crate, not one an item.
class: Work on the store's thread whose cost grows with the rows the store holds.
prevention: rebuild.rs builds the table on a worker from each pack's end at the take, and the head names those ends (invariant in the module doc, simulation tests::rebuild with the planted head). Still on the loop and of this class: the swap's walk of the delta (try_flip, end_migration) and PeriodScan listing every row; a counter of rows walked on the store's thread (IndexCounts::loop_rows) is the start of a gate for the class.
